opp_007:n1.prompt:
You are helping me provision a new workspace user account in our {{vendor}} admin console ahead of a new hire's start date. Approval is required before any change is applied to the directory, so you must prepare everything but stop short of creating the live account.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: the new hire's full legal name, personal or temp contact email (for pre-provisioning notices), intended work email/username, job title, department, manager, start date, and which groups or distribution lists they should join (e.g., team, org-wide, department groups).

Then do the following:
1. Draft the full new-user profile as it would be entered in the {{vendor}} admin console: primary email, first/last name, job title, department, manager, and any organizational unit assignment.
2. List the exact groups/mailing lists this user should be added to, based on their role/department.
3. Prepare a short checklist summarizing: account details, org unit placement, group memberships, and any licenses that should be assigned.
4. Note if drive/storage defaults or sharing settings need to be set as part of account creation, based on standard org unit defaults.
5. Do not create the user, submit the form, or make any change in the {{vendor}} admin console yourself.

When the draft profile and checklist are complete, present them to me clearly formatted (e.g., as a table or bullet list) for review, and then stop for human sign-off. I will review the details and manually create the account (or explicitly instruct you to proceed) via https://admin.google.com/.

Report back with: the finalized draft profile, the group/list assignments, any open questions (e.g., missing manager name or ambiguous department), and a one-line status such as "Ready for review — awaiting human approval to create user."

opp_007:n2.prompt:
You are helping me finish provisioning a new hire's workspace account by adding them to the correct groups and shared drives in {{vendor}}, our identity/directory platform. If you don't already have them, ask me for: the new hire's full name and email address (the account should already exist from the earlier provisioning step), their team/department, their manager or role title, and the specific group names and shared drive names they need access to (or ask me to point you to a role-based access mapping/checklist if one exists).

Using my configured credentials, please:
1. Look up the new hire's user record in {{vendor}}'s directory.
2. Identify the correct groups for their team based on the mapping I provide (or existing similar hires' group memberships if I ask you to model off a peer).
3. Add the user to each required group via the directory's group membership API or admin console.
4. Confirm whether any of these groups have dynamic membership rules or group-based app/drive assignment already configured — if so, verify the user now matches the rule instead of manually forcing membership.
5. Add the user to the specified shared drives, either directly or by confirming shared drive access is granted automatically once group membership propagates (if {{vendor}} pushes entitlements downstream via provisioning sync).
6. Re-check the user's group and shared drive membership list after changes to confirm everything applied correctly.

Done looks like: the new hire appears as a member of every required group, has access to every required shared drive, and there are no pending/failed sync errors in {{vendor}}'s admin console.

Report back with: the user's email, the final list of groups and shared drives they were added to, any groups/drives you could not add them to (with the reason), and whether access came from manual assignment or automatic group/rule-based provisioning.

opp_007:n3.prompt:
You are helping me provision SSO/SCIM app access for a new hire using our identity provider, {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for any missing details: the new hire's full name, work email/username, our company domain, the security/app groups they should join (e.g., by department or role), and which downstream apps need access (beyond Google Workspace, if any). Assume you have configured admin credentials for {{vendor}} and for Google Workspace admin.

Actions to take:
1. In {{vendor}}'s admin console, create or confirm the user's identity record with the provided email and domain.
2. Assign the user to the correct groups (using dynamic group rules if available) so app access follows group-based assignment rather than manual one-by-one grants.
3. Verify or enable SCIM provisioning for each downstream app in scope so the user, their groups, and entitlements push automatically into those apps.
4. If any required app isn't in {{vendor}}'s pre-built catalog, configure it manually via SAML/OIDC/header-based auth following {{vendor}}'s documented setup walkthrough.
5. Confirm any hire-triggered automation/workflow in {{vendor}} fires correctly for this new user (app assignment, entitlement sync).
6. Verify provisioning succeeded on the Google Workspace side by calling the Admin SDK Directory API endpoint GET /admin/directory/v1/users to confirm the new user appears with correct account status.

Done looks like: the user exists in {{vendor}}, is in the correct groups, SCIM has pushed their account into all required downstream apps, any custom app integrations are functioning, and the Google Workspace directory listing confirms the account is active.

Report back with: the user's assigned groups, list of apps provisioned via SCIM vs. manually configured, confirmation of the Google Workspace directory check, and any apps or automations that failed or need my attention.

opp_007:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the final step of provisioning a workspace account for a new hire: their first sign-in and MFA enrollment. This step cannot be completed by you or me — the new hire must personally authenticate and bind their own device, per our security policy. Your job is to prepare everything needed so the new hire can do this smoothly, then stop.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: the new hire's full name, their new workspace email address, the temporary password or sign-in method already set up for their account, our workspace provider (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Okta, etc.), and our organization's MFA policy details (which factors are allowed — authenticator app, SMS, hardware key, etc.).

Then prepare:
1. A clear, step-by-step written guide for the new hire covering: how to navigate to the sign-in page, how to log in with their temporary credentials, how to set a new password if required, and how to enroll in MFA using an approved method.
2. A short welcome message/email draft I can send them containing their workspace email, temporary credentials reference (without including the actual secret), and the enrollment guide.
3. A checklist for me to confirm before sending: correct email address, temporary password already generated and ready to hand off securely, MFA policy confirmed, and IT/security contact info included in case the new hire needs help.

Do not attempt to sign in, enter credentials, or enroll MFA on the new hire's behalf — this remains a human step that only the new hire can complete on their own device. Once your guide, message draft, and checklist are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off before anything is sent or the new hire is asked to proceed.
